sources.название: Competitive Disinhibition Mediates Behavioral Choice and Sequences in Drosophila
sources.авторы: Tihana Jovanic; Casey Martin Schneider-Mizell; Mei Shao; Jean-Baptiste Masson; Gennady Denisov; Richard Doty Fetter; Brett Daren Mensh; James William Truman; Albert Cardona; Marta Zlatic
sources.модальность: Patch-clamp neural activity, larval behaviour (hunch, bend, sequences, crawling) and serial-EM connectome reconstruction
sources.задача: Experimental circuit study of a Drosophila larval sensorimotor decision: which inhibitory interneuron motifs implement behavioural choice, maintenance and sequence transitions in response to a gentle mechanosensory (air-puff) stimulus.
sources.метод: High-throughput larval behavioural assay with automated MWT/LARA tracking of hunch, bend, crawl and transitions; targeted silencing (TNT) and optogenetic activation (CsChrimson) of mechanosensory chordotonal, Basin projection neurons and GABAergic local interneuron lines; paired whole-cell patch-clamp from Basin-1/Basin-2 in semi-dissected fillets with piezo mechanical stimuli (1000 Hz, 40 V, 10-50 ms); comprehensive serial-EM reconstruction of local interneurons in CATMAID; network modelling and connectivity analysis.
sources.датасет: Larval CNS serial-EM volume and CATMAID annotations (Janelia Fly EM; Ohyama et al., 2015; Schneider-Mizell et al., 2016) plus newly generated larval behavioural video tracked with MWT/LARA and supplemental wiring tables Data S1/S2. No data-accession number or reusable dataset identifier is reported in the article.
sources.ограничения: The stimulus is a gentle air-puff mechanosensory cue; the authors state nociceptive stimulation is absent in the freely behaving assay and present only in the dissected preparation (body-wall injury). Behavioural and electrophysiological contexts differ (proprioceptive feedback, light sensing, effective light intensity). No subjective-pain, human, ECAP or SCS measurement exists. No predictive model, cross-subject validation or reusable dataset accession is reported.

provenance.import_source: Primary publisher PDF read directly from the CC-BY archival Zenodo copy; bibliographic metadata cross-checked against Crossref and Europe PMC/MED
provenance.query_or_seed: DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2016.09.009; lead from data/audits/drosophila/drosophila-nociception-audit.json meta.candidate_reconciliation.independent_bounded_reference_list_2026_09_25.leads[9] (seed S212 R36, S769 #17)

evidence.population: Foraging third-instar larvae (72-84 h at 25 C); mechanosensory chordotonal neurons, Basin projection neurons (Basin-1, -2, -3, -4), GABAergic local interneurons (iLNa, iLNb, fbLN-Ha, fbLN-Hb) and Griddle/Handle lines; semi-dissected larval fillet preparations for electrophysiology.
evidence.sample_size: Behavioural dataset N = 1,616 larvae (Figure S1, panel H); paired patch-clamp recordings 145 trials across 16 animals (Figure S3C). Cohort sizes vary by figure.
evidence.target_label: Gentle air-puff-evoked hunch (startle), bend (exploration) and hunch-bend sequences, with Basin-1/Basin-2 patch-clamp responses and EM connectivity; explicitly not a noxious stimulus and not a pain measure.

validation.notes: Jovanic et al. (2016), Cell 167(3):858-870.e19. Access route: the complete publisher PDF (46 pages, in-press watermark) was downloaded with HTTP 200 from the CC-BY-4.0 archival copy https://zenodo.org/api/records/995631/files/article.pdf/content and read in full; the DOI landing page https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2016.09.009 resolved, while the cell.com and sciencedirect.com version-of-record pages returned HTTP 403. Crossref (HTTP 200) gave DOI, journal, volume/issue/pages, authors, year; Europe PMC/MED (HTTP 200) gave PMID 27720450 but inEPMC=N/inPMC=N, so no open publisher full text or PMC deposit exists. Results, all figures, STAR Methods, Quantification/Statistical Analysis and References were inspected. The study measures a non-noxious gentle mechanosensory air-puff: no nociceptive stimulus is applied to behaving larvae, and no human, ECAP, SCS or subjective-pain outcome is present; Drosophila larval results do not transfer to human pain. doi/pmid are metadata-level facts, not read from the article body.

sources.название: Identifying neural substrates of competitive interactions and sequence transitions during mechanosensory responses in Drosophila
sources.авторы: Jean-Baptiste Masson; François Laurent; Albert Cardona; Chloé Barré; Nicolas Skatchkovsky; Marta Zlatic; Tihana Jovanic
sources.модальность: Air-puff (mechanosensory) stimulation of freely behaving larvae; tetanus-toxin neuronal inactivation screen; MWT video tracking with machine-learning action detection; CATMAID EM reconstruction of larval CNS
sources.задача: Mechanosensory sensorimotor-choice context: identify GAL4 lines and neurons whose inactivation changes the probabilities of five discrete actions (Hunch, Bend, Back-up, Stop, Crawl) and the transitions between them after an air-puff in Drosophila larva. Not a noxious-stimulus or nociception-specific study; rolling is explicitly excluded.
sources.метод: Large-scale inactivation screen: 567 GAL4 lines (Rubin/JRC collection) plus the w;;attP2-TNT control, neurons silenced with tetanus toxin (UAS-TNT-e). Each line tested in an air-puff assay (about 50-100 larvae per plate; air-puff delivered at 45 s for 3 s; 10 pulses of 2 s from 95 s). Behaviour tracked with the Multi Worm Tracker and classified into five mutually exclusive actions by an incremental supervised-learning pipeline (random forest plus SVM layers) trained on human-tagged larval videos. Hits preselected by generalized likelihood ratio tests against the control, after removing lines with locomotor defects prior to stimulation. Candidate neurons were then matched to a CATMAID EM reconstruction of the larval CNS for connectivity. Perturbation (silencing), behaviour and EM anatomy are separate assays; no stimulus-evoked neural recording is performed.
sources.датасет: 567 GAL4 lines of the Rubin/JRC collection with expression images; behaviour of about 2.9x10^5 larvae overall, of which 13,831 w;;attP2-TNT control larvae were characterized in detail; EM wiring from a complete larval CNS serial-section TEM volume of a 6-hour-old Canton S G1 x w1118 larva, using a previously published reconstruction. The article states that all relevant data are within the manuscript and its Supporting Information files; no new public dataset accession is minted.
sources.ограничения: Mechanosensory-context study, not a nociception study: the stimulus is an air-puff and rolling (the nocifensive action) is explicitly not evoked and not analysed. Neural manipulation is tetanus-toxin silencing without stimulus-evoked neural recording, so no neural response measure is reported. Hit selection depends on statistical comparison of each line against a single control population; the authors state that hits are candidates requiring confirmation by connectome information and functional studies, and that non-hits are not excluded. No predictive model, train/test split, held-out-animal or cross-subject validation, calibration or uncertainty quantification is reported. No ECAP, no SCS, no human data and no human or clinical transfer; none may be inferred from this article.

evidence.population: Freely behaving foraging third-instar larvae; 567 GAL4 lines silenced with tetanus toxin, plus the w;;attP2-TNT control; about 2.9x10^5 larvae analysed overall, of which 13,831 w;;attP2-TNT control larvae were characterized in detail. The EM volume is from one 6-hour-old Canton S G1 x w1118 larva.
evidence.sample_size: 567 GAL4 lines screened; 95 lines removed for locomotor defects leaving 471 lines + 1 control analysed; 13,831 w;;attP2-TNT control larvae; about 2.9x10^5 larvae analysed overall; 66 candidate lines for mechanosensory responses, 25 of them for competitive interactions (abstract).
evidence.target_label: Air-puff-evoked probabilities of five discrete actions (Hunch, Bend, Back-up, Stop, Crawl) and action-transition probabilities in intact versus neuron-silenced larvae; rolling is explicitly not evoked in this assay and not studied. Not subjective pain and not a noxious-stimulus-evoked neural response.

validation.notes: Europe PMC JATS full text PMC7173939 read on 2026-09-30 (front matter, Results, Discussion, Materials and methods, Data Availability, Supporting Information list), cross-checked against the PLOS publisher manuscript JATS (HTTP 302 -> 200) and Crossref metadata (HTTP 200). Confirmed: 567 GAL4 lines screened with tetanus-toxin silencing, air-puff mechanosensory cue, machine-learning detection of five actions, MCFO/EM connectivity on a previously published larval CNS ssTEM volume, 66 candidate lines and 25 competitive-interaction lines (abstract), and 471 lines + 1 control after removing 95 locomotor-defect lines. The only occurrence of "nociceptive" in the checked text is in the action definitions ("Roll is a type of nociceptive response, that does not normally occur in response to air-puffs") and in cited literature, so the study is mechanosensory context only. Classifier accuracies are shown only in S8 Fig, which was not read, so no performance number is claimed. Stated explicitly: no noxious stimulus, no stimulus-evoked neural recording, no ECAP, no SCS, no human data, and no human or clinical transfer.

sources.авторы: Suguru Takagi; Benjamin Thomas Cocanougher; Sawako Niki; Dohjin Miyamoto; Hiroshi Kohsaka; Hokto Kazama; Richard Doty Fetter; James William Truman; Marta Zlatic; Albert Cardona; Akinao Nose
sources.модальность: Segment-specific touch-evoked behavior and somatosensory interneuron activation (head vs tail stimulation; Wave interneuron and premotor perturbation)
sources.задача: Primary experimental study of how somatosensory inputs on different larval body segments are linked to distinct motor programs: backward escape locomotion after head touch versus forward crawling after tail touch.
sources.метод: Abstract-level description only (full Methods not accessible): the authors identify a class of segmentally repeated second-order somatosensory interneurons named Wave; anterior and posterior Wave neurons extend dendrites in opposite directions to receive head and tail somatosensory input and their activation elicits backward and forward locomotion respectively; downstream premotor circuits including A03a5 are reported necessary, together with Wave, for the backward touch response. Genetic tools, preparation, imaging modality, tactile force/intensity and sample sizes are NOT verified because the article body returned HTTP 403 (subscription).
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable: descriptive developmental circuit study with no cross-subject predictive model or participant-level split
sources.ограничения: Metadata-and-abstract level only: Cell Press full text and Methods returned HTTP 403 and the article is not open access (Europe PMC inEPMC=N/inPMC=N), so stimulus intensity, preparation, imaging method, statistics and sample sizes could not be verified. The paper concerns ordinary tactile head/tail stimulation and touch-evoked locomotion, not noxious stimulation, and reports no subjective-pain measure. No ECAP, SCS, chronic-pain outcome or human data are present. Connectivity/necessity statements rest on the publisher abstract, not on checked figures. SSRN DOI 10.2139/ssrn.3155835 (same authors, 2018) is a version of the same work, not an independent source.

sources.название: Neuromuscular basis of Drosophila larval rolling escape behavior
sources.авторы: Patricia C. Cooney; Yuhan Huang; Wenze Li; Dulanjana M. Perera; Richard Hormigo; Tanya Tabachnik; Isuru S. Godage; Elizabeth M. C. Hillman; Wesley B. Grueber; Aref A. Zarin
sources.издание: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America 120(51):e2303641120
sources.модальность: High-speed volumetric SCAPE microscopy of body-wall muscle activity; optogenetic neural silencing with larval rolling assays; EM premotor-motor (PMN-MN) connectome analysis
sources.задача: Primary experimental characterization of the neuromuscular basis and candidate premotor circuits of Drosophila larval rolling escape behavior, a protective escape response triggered by class IV nociceptors or the Goro command neuron.
sources.метод: Custom high-speed volumetric SCAPE microscope imaged body-wall muscle activity during rolling. Rolling was induced by optogenetic activation of Goro (Goro-LexA>lexAop-Chrimson) or nociceptors; subsets of motor neurons were acutely silenced with Gal4-driven GtACR1-eGFP. PMN-MN connectivity was analyzed from previously published EM connectome raw data (Zarin et al.) with a shuffling control for dorsoventral structure. Behavioral readout was completion of at least one 360-degree roll.
sources.датасет: Drosophila melanogaster larvae (L1, L2, L3) in optogenetic rolling assays; per-genotype animal counts are reported only graphically in Fig. 4C. PMN-MN connectome raw data reused from the Zarin et al. eLife dataset. Analysis scripts and 3D larva model: https://github.com/cooneypc4/larval_escape_manuscript
sources.производительность: Fig. 4C rolling success/defect: silencing VL/DO type Ib MNs (HB9-Gal4, vGlut-AD-Nkx6-DBD) abolished bending and rolling; DL type Ib MN silencing gave 25% (L1) and 13% (L3) failure with CQ-Gal4, but 68% (L1/L2) and 42% (L3) defects with Unc4-AD-vGlut-DBD; silencing type Is MNs (R27E09) had little/no effect; combined DL Ib+Is silencing (CQ+RRa) caused severe failure; A02-PMN silencing (per-Gal4) produced 93% rolling defects. No confidence intervals or single pooled denominator are reported.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable
sources.ограничения: Measures an objective larval escape/rolling motor program: nociceptor or Goro activation is a trigger, not a subjective pain measure. No ECAP, spinal-cord stimulation, clinical outcome or human data are present (0 hits for ECAP/SCS/human in the checked full text). The PMN-MN connectome is reanalyzed from a previously published dataset and its link to rolling is correlational/model-based; A02-PMN silencing uses per-Gal4 with possible off-target expression, so it does not isolate single PMNs. Per-genotype sample sizes and uncertainty are not numerically reported.

provenance.import_source: PNAS primary full text via publisher-deposited Europe PMC JATS (PMC10743538); publisher landing returned HTTP 403
provenance.query_or_seed: DOI 10.1073/pnas.2303641120; exact DOI/title/PMID/PMCID duplicate check in records.json and aliases.json

evidence.population: Drosophila larvae (L1, L2, L3) in optogenetic rolling assays; body-wall muscles and larval MNs/PMNs from EM connectome data
evidence.sample_size: Rolling assays: per-genotype animal counts shown only graphically in Fig. 4C (L1/L2 and L3, exact numbers not given in the text). SCAPE muscle-activity analysis: forward crawling n=2 crawls/2 larvae/86 muscles vs rolling n=4 rolls/3 larvae/372 muscles (Fig. 2F); bent-vs-stretched side n=3 rolls/3 larvae/280 muscles (Fig. 2-related caption). Escape-pattern histograms: n=64 rolls (Goro optogenetic) and n=47 rolls (heat+vibration) (Fig. 1). No single pooled denominator.
evidence.target_label: Rolling escape motor program: circumferential muscle-contraction progression and candidate premotor-motor connectivity; nociception is the activating trigger, not a subjective pain measure.

validation.notes: PNAS primary full text checked via Europe PMC JATS PMC10743538 (Results, Discussion, Materials and Methods, Data Availability). Publisher landing (pnas.org) returned HTTP 403; PubMed/Europe PMC gave PMID 38096410 / PMCID PMC10743538. The bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2023.02.01.526733 is the same study, not an independent replication. No ECAP, SCS or human transfer.

sources.название: The motor pattern of rolling escape locomotion in Drosophila larvae
sources.авторы: Liping He; Lydia J. Borjon; W. Daniel Tracey
sources.издание: Journal of Experimental Biology (J Exp Biol) 229(17): jeb252063
sources.модальность: GCaMP6f calcium imaging of larval body-wall muscles with optogenetic cIVda nociceptor activation (ppk-GAL4>UAS-ChR2), plus analysis of a published premotor-to-motor-neuron connectome
sources.задача: Primary experimental study determining the body-wall muscle activation sequence that generates rolling escape locomotion in Drosophila larvae, with a motor-network connectivity analysis.
sources.метод: Second-instar Drosophila larvae with muscle GCaMP6f (R44H10-LexA LexAop-GCaMP6f) and cIVda-specific ChR2::YFP (ppk1.9-GAL4); a 488 nm laser both excited GCaMP and optogenetically triggered rolling. A high-speed inverted confocal time-lapse preparation imaged muscle activity at 60 frames s-1 for about 10 s, viewing roughly half the larval circumference (119.5 um section in a ~250 um larva). Muscle ON/OFF was scored frame by frame across abdominal segments A1-A7; visual scoring was validated by ROI dF/F on DL9, DL4 and VA26 in A4. Activation timing was normalized to a rolling cycle (NTime 0 = ventral midline of A4 centred, 0.5 = dorsal midline, 1 = full 360 deg roll). Co-active groups were derived from pairwise distances between activation curves. The motor-neuron connectivity network was computed from the published Zarin et al. (2019) PMN-to-MN matrix (one-mode projection), with Louvain community detection and a 1000-sample permutation test.
sources.ограничения: Optogenetic cIVda activation replaced a natural noxious stimulus; roll duration was 1.60+/-0.36 s (mean+/-s.d., n=9) clockwise and 1.70+/-0.46 s (n=10) counterclockwise. Imaging resolved only about half the larva at a time, muscles could not be tracked once they entered the C-bend, and no individual-larva count is stated (19 completed rolls total). Nineteen of 23 rolls were biased toward the coverslip/light side, so exiting-phase muscles were rarely sampled. Weakly activated muscles may have been missed. The connectivity network is a conceptual reanalysis of a published A1-segment connectome, not new anatomy, and is not functionally validated. No ECAP, SCS, human pain or clinical transfer is reported.

evidence.sample_size: 19 rolling recordings with completed rolls (9 clockwise, 10 counterclockwise); number of individual larvae not stated.
evidence.target_label: Muscle activation sequence (GCaMP6f ON/OFF) across larval body-wall muscles during optogenetically triggered rolling escape; a motor program, not a pain report.

Europe PMC JATS full text PMC13615696 (HTTP 200) checked; the publisher DOI page returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare challenge), so the full-text route was Europe PMC. Records 11 of 30 body-wall muscles consistently recruited as four co-active groups in a circumferential wave, with a ring-like conceptual MN network. No subjective pain, human, ECAP or SCS measure.

sources.название: Serotonergic Modulation Enables Pathway-Specific Plasticity in a Developing Sensory Circuit in Drosophila
sources.авторы: Takuya Kaneko; Ann Marie Macara; Ruonan Li; Yujia Hu; Kenichi Iwasaki; Zane Dunnings; Ethan Firestone; Shawn Horvatic; Ananya Guntur; Orie T. Shafer; Chung-Hui Yang; Jie Zhou; Bing Ye
sources.модальность: Larval rolling/curling behavior; GCaMP6f calcium imaging and Epac1-camps cAMP imaging in dissected larval ventral nerve cord; optogenetic (ChR2/CsChrimson) and chemogenetic (P2X2/ATP) stimulation; AITC chemical stimulation; single-neuron FLP-out mosaic labeling and syb-GRASP connectivity
sources.задача: Determine how noxious sensory experience during development produces long-lasting, sensory-pathway-specific plasticity in the Drosophila larval nociceptive circuit, and identify the serotonergic feedback motif that mediates it.
sources.метод: Larvae reared on AITC (2.5-5 mM) or with optogenetic C4da stimulation during development; rolling/curling scored in mature wandering 3rd-instar larvae under optogenetic or AITC stimulation. GCaMP6f calcium imaging and Epac1-camps cAMP imaging of C4da axon terminals, A08n and Basin-4 neurons in dissected larvae with ATP/P2X2 or AITC stimulation. TRH-GAL4 serotonergic silencing (Kir2.1), 5-HTP feeding and developmental CsChrimson stimulation of serotonergic neurons. syb-GRASP connectivity and FLP-out single-neuron labeling. Statistics: chi-squared for behavior, Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis for imaging/length; SEM error bars.
sources.датасет: Drosophila melanogaster wandering 3rd-instar larval cohorts (both sexes) for behavioral, optogenetic, AITC and 5-HTP assays, plus separate dissected larval ventral-nerve-cord preparations for calcium/cAMP imaging. Per-figure N of larvae is stated in the legends; no reusable numeric dataset is deposited.
sources.производительность: Fig. 4D: 5-HTP feeding throughout development produced a 2-fold reduction in rolling (n=135 vs 105 larvae); Fig. 4E: 5-HTP on days 1-2 likewise a 2-fold reduction (n=50 vs 60). Fig. 4B: TRH>Kir2.1 silencing partially rescued rolling after developmental nociceptor stimulation (n=120/120/135/120). Fig. 1E: developmental stimulation lowered the maximal optogenetic rolling response across five test intensities (n=115/88/69). Endpoints are group percentages/proportions and optical ΔF/F0, not a predictive-model metric.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable: mechanistic larval circuit experiment with group-level behavioral and optical-imaging readouts; no participant-level predictive model or cross-subject generalization test.
sources.ограничения: Behavior, dissected-larva calcium/cAMP imaging and optogenetic/chemogenetic stimulation are separate preparations that must not be pooled. GCaMP6f and Epac1-camps are optical reporters, not electrophysiological spike records. Nocifensive rolling/curling, A08n and Basin-4 responses, and serotonin/cAMP signaling do not measure subjective pain. Larval serotonergic manipulation establishes no human, ECAP or SCS transfer. Per-figure N of larvae differ and no single combined cohort size exists. An erratum (DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2017.07.023, Neuron 95(3):722) is registered by Crossref, but its full text was not accessible in this pass (cell.com returned HTTP 403/anti-bot).

provenance.import_source: SRC-04 primary route 2026-09-30: PMC author manuscript PMC5555049 retrieved via NCBI efetch (eutils efetch.fcgi db=pmc, HTTP 200) after the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returned HTTP 500; Crossref metadata HTTP 200.
provenance.query_or_seed: Exact DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2017.06.034 (Neuron 95(3):623-638.e4); PMC5555049 author manuscript via NCBI efetch; Crossref record and Crossref erratum 10.1016/j.neuron.2017.07.023.

evidence.population: Wandering 3rd-instar larvae (both sexes) for behavioral, optogenetic, AITC and 5-HTP assays; dissected larval ventral-nerve-cord preparations for calcium/cAMP imaging. Cells of interest: C4da nociceptors, A08n and Basin-4 second-order neurons, TRH serotonergic neurons.
evidence.sample_size: Per-figure N of larvae; e.g., Fig. 1C n=75 per group, Fig. 1D n=45 per group, Fig. 1E n=115/88/69, Fig. 4B n=120/120/135/120, Fig. 4D n=135/105, Fig. 4E n=50/60, Fig. 4G n=27/23 neurons. No single combined cohort size.
evidence.target_label: Noxious-input-induced, pathway-specific plasticity: developmental AITC or optogenetic C4da stimulation suppresses later larval rolling/curling, with A08n/Basin-4 calcium and serotonergic (TRH) circuit/cAMP readouts. Not subjective pain.

validation.notes: Kaneko et al. (2017), Neuron 95(3):623-638.e4; PMC author manuscript PMC5555049 read end to end (Summary, Introduction, Results/Figs. 1-6, Discussion, STAR Methods, figure legends). Behavioral rolling/curling, dissected-larva GCaMP6f calcium and Epac1-camps cAMP imaging, and optogenetic/chemogenetic stimulation are kept as separate assays. Confirmed: developmental noxious input (AITC or optogenetic C4da) suppresses later nociceptive behavior; A08n receives nociceptor but not mechanosensor input; TRH serotonergic feedback inhibits C4da-to-A08n transmission. Identifiers cross-checked against Crossref (DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2017.06.034, PMID 28712652, Neuron 95(3):623-638.e4). An erratum is registered (DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2017.07.023); its text was not accessible this pass. No subjective-pain, human ECAP or SCS outcome is reported.

sources.название: Light-avoidance-mediating photoreceptors tile the Drosophila larval body wall
sources.авторы: Yang Xiang; Quan Yuan; Nina Vogt; Loren L Looger; Lily Yeh Jan; Yuh Nung Jan
sources.модальность: Light-evoked class IV dendritic arborization neuron calcium/somatic activity and action potentials, with separate larval light-avoidance behavior
sources.задача: Primary experimental study showing that Drosophila larval class IV dendritic arborization (c4da) neurons, described as nociceptors, are activated by ultraviolet, violet and blue light, that their dendrites tile the larval body wall, and that they mediate larval light avoidance; the studied stimulus is light, not a noxious stimulus.
sources.метод: Single-larva light-avoidance assay scored reversal or head-turning away from a 1.7-mm light spot during 5-s illumination, using white light and bandpass filters (360/402/470/525/620 nm; ~0.57 mW mm-2 and higher). Separate neural assays: GCaMP3 calcium imaging of dorsal, lateral and ventral class IV dendritic arborization (da) neurons (ddaC, V'ada, VdaB) in third-instar fillets on a Zeiss LSM510 META confocal with 488-nm excitation; extracellular recordings of ddaC action potentials with an Axon 700B amplifier; and primary embryonic class IV/III da neuron cultures. Genetics used GAL4/UAS, MARCM and P-element/RNAi lines for Gr28b and TrpA1. Calcium imaging and electrophysiology are neural measures; the light-avoidance behavioral cohorts are separate animals.
sources.ограничения: The primary stimulus is light, so no noxious-stimulus-evoked nociceptive response is the target of the study; class IV neurons are only described as candidate nociceptors from prior work. Noxious heat (>40 degC) and allyl isothiocyanate appear only as supplementary controls to exclude thermal and ROS confounds. Neural and behavioral cohorts are separate preparations. Per-figure n values are reported but no single combined sample size and no reusable dataset or predictive metrics. No human, ECAP or clinical SCS data; animal-to-human transfer is not established.

provenance.import_source: primary full-text route; open PMC author manuscript PMC3026603 checked directly
provenance.query_or_seed: doi 10.1038/nature09576 (find exact title)

evidence.population: Drosophila third-instar larvae; class IV dendritic arborization (c4da/ddaC) neurons and whole-larva behavior
evidence.sample_size: Per-assay cohorts: n=5-16 neurons/cells in imaging and electrophysiology figures; 20-40 larvae per light-avoidance condition; no single combined sample size.
evidence.target_label: Larval light-avoidance behavior plus light-evoked class IV da neuron calcium and action-potential responses. Light is not a defined thermal, mechanical or chemical noxious stimulus, and no subjective-pain measure is present.

validation.notes: Xiang et al. (2010), Nature 468(7326):921-926. Full text checked via the open PMC author manuscript (PMC3026603; HTTP 200 on 2026-09-30); the publisher Nature page returns only a subscription preview, and the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returned HTTP 500 on retry. Class IV da neurons (ddaC, V'ada, VdaB) show light-evoked GCaMP3 calcium signals and extracellular spike increases in an intensity- and wavelength-dependent manner, and larvae avoid bright short-wavelength light; Gr28b and TrpA1 are required. This card is cross-modal nociceptor/context evidence only. It cannot support subjective pain, human transfer, ECAP recruitment or clinical SCS response claims.

sources.название: The Ionotropic Receptors IR21a and IR25a mediate cool sensing in Drosophila
sources.авторы: Lina Ni; Mason Klein; Kathryn V Svec; Gonzalo Budelli; Elaine C Chang; Anggie J Ferrer; Richard Benton; Aravinthan DT Samuel; Paul A Garrity
sources.модальность: Larval thermotaxis behavior; GCaMP6m calcium imaging of larval Dorsal Organ Cool Cells (DOCCs) and adult arista thermoreceptors; IR25a immunohistochemistry; genetic loss-of-function and rescue analysis.
sources.задача: Primary experimental physiology study: determine the molecular receptors that mediate cool sensing in Drosophila, specifically whether Ionotropic Receptors IR21a and IR25a are required for DOCC cool detection and larval cool avoidance.
sources.метод: Thermotaxis of early 2nd instar larvae tracked for 15 min on a 13.5-21.5 C gradient (~0.36 C/cm), quantified as navigational bias (Tukey HSD behavioral statistics). DOCC and adult arista responses measured with genetically encoded GCaMP6m calcium imaging under sinusoidal temperature stimuli (larval ~14-20 C; adult 14-30 C), analysed with Steel-Dwass tests; IR25a immunostaining; Ir21a and Ir25a loss-of-function alleles with genomic and Gal4-driven rescue; ectopic IR21a expression in adult Hot Cell neurons, including in Gr28b mutant background.
sources.ограничения: This is a Drosophila larval and adult cool-sensing molecular study. The primary endpoint is larval cool avoidance (protective behavior) and calcium signals in thermosensory neurons, not nociception or pain. No noxious-heat assay, no subjective pain measure, and no human, ECAP, SCS or clinical transfer is evaluated. Heterologous expression of IR21a/IR25a in S2 cells, Xenopus oocytes and HEK cells failed to yield cooling responses (unpublished), so the receptor mechanism is not reconstituted in a heterologous system. Sample sizes are figure- and assay-specific (e.g. thermotaxis wild type n=836 animals; imaging Ns per genotype); no pooled sample or cross-subject predictive validation is reported.

evidence.population: Early 2nd instar D. melanogaster larvae for thermotaxis and DOCC calcium imaging; adult arista thermoreceptors (Hot Cells and Cold Cells) for adult calcium imaging.
evidence.sample_size: Figure- and assay-specific. Thermotaxis navigational bias: wild type n=836 animals, Ir21a mutants/rescues and Ir25a mutants n=10-247 per genotype. DOCC imaging: wild type n=33 cells (11 animals), Ir21a mutants/rescues and Ir25a mutants n=30-58 cells per genotype. Adult Hot Cell imaging: wild type n=11-16 cells, ectopic-IR21a and mutant groups n=9-25 cells. No single pooled sample.
evidence.target_label: Larval cool avoidance (navigational bias away from ~13.5 C toward warmer temperatures) plus calcium responses of cool-sensing DOCCs and adult Hot Cell neurons; not nociception or subjective pain.

This is a cool-thermosensation molecular study with a protective-behavior endpoint; no subjective-pain or human/ECAP/SCS transfer is supported.

sources.название: Sound response mediated by the TRP channels NOMPC, NANCHUNG, and INACTIVE in chordotonal organs of Drosophila larvae
sources.авторы: Wei Zhang; Zhiqiang Yan; Lily Yeh Jan; Yuh Nung Jan
sources.издание: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (PNAS) 110(33):13612-13617; published online 29 July 2013, issue date 13 August 2013
sources.модальность: Sound/vibration-evoked startle and burrowing behavior; extracellular single-unit action-potential recording from severed body-wall nerve bundles; in vivo GCaMP5 calcium imaging of chordotonal (Cho) and da neurons; anti-NOMPC immunostaining
sources.задача: Test whether Drosophila larvae detect and respond to natural sounds and pure tones, identify which sensory organs (chordotonal organs, class I-IV da neurons) are required for the behavioral response, and determine which mechanotransduction channels (NOMPC, NANCHUNG, INACTIVE, dmPIEZO) mediate the Cho sound response.
sources.метод: Third-instar larvae on an agar plate placed above a speaker were stimulated with 1-s pure-tone pulses (e.g., 500 Hz, 70 dB) repeated 10 times and scored for startle (pause, mouth-hook retraction, turning, backward locomotion); burrowing was scored as the number of larvae with more than half the body exposed on the food surface. Tetrahydrotoxin (TNT) expression in Cho and class I/III/IV da neurons blocked synaptic output. Extracellular recordings used suction/glass electrodes on severed body-wall nerve bundles and identified Cho neurons by IAV-Gal4 or NOMPC-Gal4 markers. In vivo GCaMP5 calcium imaging of Cho neurons was performed on larvae pressed between coverslips, with delta-F/F0 referenced to the 5 s before stimulus. Mutants (nompC, iav1, nan1, dmpiezo) and rescue (UAS-NOMPC in Cho) tested channel dependence. Unpaired t tests were used.
sources.датасет: Primary experimental observations and SI figures/movies in the article; no dataset accession or repository deposit was identified in the checked text. Cohorts are per figure (e.g., Fig. 1B startle scores n = 7, 7, 7, 5, 8, 7 across genotype groups; Fig. 1D n = 7); behavior, calcium imaging and electrophysiology use separate preparations and sample sizes and must not be pooled.
sources.производительность: Not a predictive model; no predictive performance metrics. Experimental outcomes are reported as startle response scores (sum over 10 stimulus presentations), counts of larvae remaining on the food surface, action-potential spike counts/firing rate, and GCaMP delta-F/F0, with per-figure unpaired t tests and SEM error bars.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_reported
sources.ограничения: The central endpoint is sound/vibration-evoked startle and burrowing, not noxious mechanical or thermal nociception; relevance to the nociception corpus is mechanistic/contextual. Body-wall class IV da neurons only partially reduce the startle response and are not directly sound-excited. There is no human, ECAP or SCS data and no clinical or human-pain transfer; larval startle does not establish subjective pain. Sample sizes are per-figure and are not a single pooled cohort, and no dataset accession was identified.

provenance.import_source: Primary PNAS research article read directly from the PMC free full text (PMC3746866, HTTP 200); Europe PMC/PubMed records used for bibliographic metadata and identifiers.
provenance.query_or_seed: DOI 10.1073/pnas.1312477110 (S840 reference R19 lead); verified against PMC3746866 full text and Crossref/Europe PMC metadata; checked 2026-09-30

evidence.population: Mid-third-instar D. melanogaster larvae, wild-type and mutant/transgenic lines (nompC, iav1, nan1, dmpiezo; TNT and Gal4 lines). Behavioral, calcium-imaging and electrophysiological assays use separate larval preparations; per-figure sample sizes are small (e.g., n = 5-8 per genotype group).
evidence.sample_size: Figure-specific and not pooled: Fig. 1B startle response n = 7, 7, 7, 5, 8, 7 across genotype groups and * P < 0.001 (unpaired t test); Fig. 1D burrowing n = 7. Calcium imaging and electrophysiology report single-cell or small-n recordings rather than one overall cohort.
evidence.target_label: Sound/vibration-evoked larval startle and burrowing escape behavior, with Cho-neuron action-potential firing and GCaMP calcium response as the mechanosensory readouts. Not a noxious-stimulus or subjective-pain measure.

validation.notes: Zhang et al. (2013), PNAS 110(33):13612-13617, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1312477110, PMID 23898199. Full text read directly from the PMC free full text (PMC3746866, HTTP 200): abstract, Results (Figs. 1-4), Discussion and Materials and Methods, including behavioral scoring, imaging, electrophysiology, mutants and statistics. Bibliographic fields and identifiers confirmed via Crossref (HTTP 200) and Europe PMC (HTTP 200). Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 on 4 retries and the NCBI efetch PMC XML route returned only front matter ("publisher does not allow downloading of the full text in XML form"), so the checked route was the PMC HTML article. The paper concerns sound/vibration sensing and its TRP-channel basis, not noxious nociception; this is a related but distinct modality from S839 cold nociception. No ECAP, SCS, human or clinical-transfer evidence, and no dataset accession identified.

sources.название: Drosophila NOMPC is a mechanotransduction channel subunit for gentle-touch sensation
sources.авторы: Zhiqiang Yan; Wei Zhang; Ye He; David Gorczyca; Yang Xiang; Li E. Cheng; Shan Meltzer; Lily Yeh Jan; Yuh Nung Jan
sources.издание: Nature 493(7431):221-225; published online 9 December 2012, print 10 January 2013; author manuscript PMC3917554
sources.модальность: Mechanical body-wall displacement (eyelash gentle touch; piezo-actuator probe; negative pressure on excised patch); extracellular action-potential recording from larval class III and class IV da neurons; GCaMP5 calcium imaging; NOMPC immunostaining; heterologous NOMPC expression and patch-clamp in Drosophila S2 cells.
sources.задача: Determine which sensory neurons and mechanotransduction channel mediate gentle-touch sensation in Drosophila larvae, and test whether NOMPC is required in class III da neurons and sufficient to confer touch sensitivity when ectopically expressed.
sources.метод: Eyelash gentle-touch behavioural scoring in intact larvae from the established assay; TNT silencing of class III da neurons; extracellular recordings from class III/IV da neurons in fillet preparations with calibrated 10-40 um body-wall displacements; GCaMP5 calcium imaging; NOMPC immunostaining; nompC and iav mutants with class III neuronal rescue; ectopic NOMPC in class IV/class I neurons; whole-cell and outside-out patch recordings of NOMPC-expressing S2 cells with piezo-probe displacement, high-speed pressure clamp and pore-residue mutagenesis (E1511, D1516).
sources.датасет: No reusable dataset or accession number is reported; results are figure-level experimental observations. Figure-specific sample sizes are recorded in evidence.sample_size.
sources.производительность: Not a predictive model; no predictive performance metric. Outcomes are action-potential counts, GCaMP5 calcium responses, scored gentle-touch behaviour and S2-cell single-channel/current measurements, with figure-specific tests (unpaired t-test; one-way ANOVA with Tukey; P values) and +/- s.e.m.
sources.кросс_субъект: Not a prediction or generalization study; no held-out-larva or cross-subject validation split is reported.
sources.ограничения: The measured construct is gentle-touch (non-noxious, low-threshold) mechanosensation; the paper explicitly reports that the same gentle-touch stimulus did not activate class IV mechanical nociceptors, so this is not a noxious-stimulus nociception assay. Peripheral neural and behavioural observables are not subjective pain. The S2-cell system is an in vitro heterologous mechanotransduction assay. No ECAP, SCS or human transfer is evaluated; no dataset accession and no cross-subject validation are reported. Figure n are assay-specific and must not be pooled.

Ectopic NOMPC and S2-cell channels are separate manipulations. Not a noxious-stimulus nociception assay and not a measure of subjective pain.

Verbatim limits: the tested gentle-touch stimulus did not excite class IV mechanical nociceptors, and the study contains no ECAP, SCS or human data. No dataset accession was found in the checked text. It is therefore recorded as relevance 3, included_context, verified_primary.

sources.название: Cross-species connectome comparisons reveal the network attributes of memory capacity and time series prediction
sources.авторы: Yazhe Yan; Geyang Wu; Haoming Yu; Qilin She; Yu Qian
sources.издание: bioRxiv preprint v1, posted 31 October 2025; DOI 10.1101/2025.10.29.685101; no peer-reviewed version of record confirmed on the checked routes
sources.модальность: Empirical structural connectomes (fruit fly, mouse, rat, macaque) and human functional connectomes (cognitively normal, Alzheimer's disease) used as echo-state-network recurrent matrices; simulated reservoir dynamics, Lorenz and Mackey-Glass prediction MSE, and memory capacity
sources.задача: Test whether empirical connectome topology gives echo state networks an advantage in chaotic time-series prediction and memory capacity, and whether weak-tie nodes and Alzheimer's-disease connectomes change that performance
sources.метод: Echo state networks whose recurrent weight matrix is a spectral-radius-scaled empirical connectome (W_bio = alpha * W_0); ridge-regression readout; Lorenz and Mackey-Glass prediction and input-recall memory capacity; randomly shuffled weight controls; weak-tie removal and weak-to-strong conversion perturbations; AD versus cognitively normal functional connectomes as reservoirs
sources.датасет: Conn2Res toolbox connectomes for fruit fly, mouse, rat and macaque; pre-processed human functional connectomes (cognitively normal and Alzheimer's disease) from the Auckland brain-network collection, DOI 10.17608/K6.AUCKLAND.21397377; perturbation experiments use n=10 networks per species
sources.производительность: Phylogenetic order macaque > rat > mouse > fly: macaque gave the lowest Lorenz MSE and the highest memory capacity around spectral scaling alpha ~ 1; native connectomes beat shuffled controls (paired t-test, p < 0.01 for all species); weak-tie removal and weak-to-strong conversion raised MSE and lowered MC (two-way ANOVA, p < 0.001); AD connectomes showed higher MSE and lower MC than cognitively normal connectomes (t-test, p < 0.01). Exact MSE and MC numbers are printed only in figures and were not extracted as numeric values.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable
sources.ограничения: In-silico study only. No human ECAP, no SCS, no pain construct, no clinical outcome and no validated fly/animal-to-human transfer is tested; the human AD comparison is a group-averaged functional-connectome simulation, and the checked text gives no participant counts, no subject-level split and no independent external cohort. Connectomes differ in spatial scale and resolution, the model is static (no synaptic plasticity, no delays), and the descriptive cross-species ordering is not an inter-species predictive transfer. This is bioRxiv v1 with no confirmed peer-reviewed version of record. Equations and figures were images and were not read as numbers; the article states no Data or Code availability section.

evidence.population: Empirical connectome matrices from four model species and pre-processed human functional connectomes (cognitively normal and Alzheimer's disease) deployed in silico as echo-state-network reservoirs; no new animals or humans were enrolled.

All experiments are in silico: the 5:80:15 warmup-train-validate split is over time steps of each series, and the shuffling/weak-tie perturbations are internal controls, not an independent cohort. No v2 or journal version of record was confirmed (bioRxiv API lists version 1 with published NA; later version rechecks were rate-limited, HTTP 429). sources.название: Non-random brain connectome wiring enables robust and efficient neural network function under high sparsity
sources.авторы: James McAllister; Conor Houghton; John Wade; Cian O'Donnell
sources.издание: bioRxiv preprint (openRxiv / Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory), v1 posted 1 April 2026; DOI 10.64898/2026.03.30.715411; CC BY 4.0
sources.модальность: Connectome-derived Echo State Network (fixed recurrent reservoir) simulations of larval and adult hemibrain Drosophila connectomes with synthetic task inputs, simulated reservoir activity and linear readouts; no biological recording modality
sources.задача: Test how extremely sparse biological wiring can support robust and efficient computation: compare connectome-based Echo State Networks (CoNNs) against sparsity-matched random networks on eight reservoir tasks under structured neuron pruning and hyperparameter variation
sources.метод: Echo State Networks whose fixed reservoir is the topology of larval and adult hemibrain Drosophila connectome subgraphs obtained by hierarchical stochastic block model decomposition (communities of 100-400 neurons; 9 larval and 28 adult connectome ESNs, 30 weight randomisations each); weights sampled uniformly from [-1, 1] and rescaled to spectral radius 0.99; leaky tanh state update with ridge-regression readout; null models are sparsity-matched Erdos-Renyi graphs and configuration-model graphs with matched degree distributions; eight tasks in four categories (working memory, decision-making, time-series prediction, chaotic time-series prediction), two task types each; structured pruning in order of weighted task variance; maximum Lyapunov exponent, Lyapunov dimension, PCA dimensionality and mean pairwise correlation measures; analytic scaling of spectral radius under pruning and random networks with controlled self-connection fraction q; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests
sources.датасет: Larval (Winding et al. 2023) and adult hemibrain (Scheffer et al. 2020) Drosophila melanogaster connectomes, mean wiring sparsity 0.9859 (larva) and 0.9802 (adult); connectome-derived subnetworks of 100-400 neurons with 30 weight instantiations each; no new dataset or dataset identifier is released by the authors; code and data are placed at https://github.com/jajmcallister/Conn_ESN_Paper/
sources.производительность: Model-only comparison, no clinical or accuracy endpoint. CoNNs showed lower mean participation ratio of weighted task variance, i.e. narrower task engagement, than random networks (p = 0.004 larva and p < 0.001 adult), and higher local clustering and self-recurrency in the same comparisons. Robustness is summarised as the fraction of the network removed before a 10 percent relative performance drop: CoNNs were as robust or more robust than random networks for all eight tasks (Figure S18). Increasing the self-connection fraction q from 0.04 to 0.2 systematically slowed the decay of relative spectral radius under random pruning and matched the theoretical approximation. Continuous curves and per-task values are figure-level, not tabulated in the text.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable: in-silico connectome reservoir comparison with no participants, no live animals and no cross-subject or cross-species prediction task
sources.ограничения: Preprint, not peer reviewed in a journal. Model-only: biological realism is reduced to a weighted adjacency matrix with weights sampled from a uniform distribution and a simple tanh nonlinearity, so wiring is treated as a structural scaffold rather than a measured dynamical system. The adult networks use the hemibrain (one central-brain hemisphere) rather than the full brain, and subnetworks come from a model-dependent hierarchical stochastic block model, so they may not correspond to functional units of the living brain. No nociceptive, noxious stimulus, ECAP, SCS, chronic-pain or human construct is measured or tested, and no Drosophila-to-human transfer is established; the checked text contains no pain, clinical or human-participant analysis. No cross-subject or independent external validation is possible.

производительность.value: Model-only comparison, no clinical or accuracy endpoint. CoNNs showed lower mean participation ratio of weighted task variance, i.e. narrower task engagement, than random networks (p = 0.004 larva and p < 0.001 adult), and higher local clustering and self-recurrency in the same comparisons. Robustness is summarised as the fraction of the network removed before a 10 percent relative performance drop: CoNNs were as robust or more robust than random networks for all eight tasks (Figure S18). Increasing the self-connection fraction q from 0.04 to 0.2 systematically slowed the decay of relative spectral radius under random pruning and matched the theoretical approximation. Continuous curves and per-task values are figure-level, not tabulated in the text.

ограничения.value: Preprint, not peer reviewed in a journal. Model-only: biological realism is reduced to a weighted adjacency matrix with weights sampled from a uniform distribution and a simple tanh nonlinearity, so wiring is treated as a structural scaffold rather than a measured dynamical system. The adult networks use the hemibrain (one central-brain hemisphere) rather than the full brain, and subnetworks come from a model-dependent hierarchical stochastic block model, so they may not correspond to functional units of the living brain. No nociceptive, noxious stimulus, ECAP, SCS, chronic-pain or human construct is measured or tested, and no Drosophila-to-human transfer is established; the checked text contains no pain, clinical or human-participant analysis. No cross-subject or independent external validation is possible.

sources.название: Mouse to Human Cross-Species Transfer Learning for Electrophysiology-to-Transcriptomics Mapping in Cortical GABAergic Interneurons
sources.авторы: Theo Schwider; Ramin Ramezani
sources.модальность: Patch-seq current-clamp electrophysiology (IPFX features, 12 feature families) paired with transcriptomic GABAergic interneuron subclass labels (Lamp5, Pvalb, Sst, Vip, Sncg); NWB recordings from Allen Institute mouse visual cortex and human neurosurgical neocortex.
sources.задача: Reproduce the Gouwens IPFX/sPCA random-forest baseline for transcriptomic subclass prediction and test mouse-to-human cross-species transfer learning on an aligned 4-class interneuron task.
sources.метод: IPFX (v2.1.2) feature extraction into 12 feature families; sparse PCA (44 sPCs) plus a class-balanced random-forest baseline; attention-based BiLSTM over the family-vector tensor (no sPCA); class weighting, SMOTE (train-only) and an ArcFace variant; joint shared-encoder two-head mouse+human pretraining followed by human-only fine-tuning; mouse 60/20/20 hold-out and human 5-fold stratified cross-validation.
sources.датасет: Allen Institute public Patch-seq data via DANDI: DANDI:000020 mouse visual cortex (version 0.210913.1639, 3,699 neurons after QC) and DANDI:000636 human interneuron Patch-seq (version 0.241120.0510, 506 neurons after QC), plus the human_patchseq_gaba metadata repository associated with Lee et al. (2023).
sources.производительность: Mouse random forest 0.8728 macro-F1 / 90.72% accuracy; mouse ArcFace BiLSTM+attention+SMOTE 0.8869 +/- 0.0186 macro-F1 and 0.9212 accuracy (Table 4) while the Results text states 0.8923 / 0.9235 for the same configuration, an unresolved internal inconsistency. Human random forest 0.6589 macro-F1 / 75.18% accuracy; human BiLSTM+attention 0.6685 +/- 0.0141. Transfer learning on the aligned 4-class task: human-only baseline 0.6580 +/- 0.0286 -> mouse-pretrained 0.6795 +/- 0.0120 macro-F1; accuracy 0.7710 +/- 0.0172 -> 0.7905 +/- 0.0096.
sources.ограничения: The only human data are 506 public Allen Institute Patch-seq neurons from anonymized neurosurgical resections; no donor, session, cortical-area or batch variable is reported, and donor-held-out generalisation is not tested, so the reported human 5-fold cross-validation may share donors between training and evaluation folds. The two Tables 4/5 and Results text disagree on the best mouse ArcFace numbers. The mouse-to-human transfer gain (about +0.02 macro-F1) is small, single-direction and evaluated only within the same public dataset. Code and harmonized metadata are announced as placeholders (GitHub link not yet populated). No human ECAP, SCS treatment, chronic-pain, nociception or clinical outcome is measured or predicted; transfer to human pain or SCS use is not shown by this paper and must not be assumed.

The VOR registers no has-preprint, so the VOR<->preprint link is author-declared here. Preprint title is inverted ("Human to Mouse") versus the VOR title ("Mouse to Human"), and the preprint abstract says the work "replicates and extends" Gouwens whereas the VOR abstract says it "adapts the IPFX/Gouwens feature-family organization"; the two abstracts otherwise match. Because the VOR body text is paywalled, methods/results recorded here come from the author preprint v1 and were not re-checked against the VOR, hence metadata_only rather than checked. Within the preprint, Table 4 gives the best mouse ArcFace configuration 0.8869 +/- 0.0186 macro-F1 while the Results narrative states 0.8923 for the same configuration - an internal inconsistency left unresolved. sources.название: Electrophysiologic Characteristics of Epidural Spinal Signals in Preclinical Models of Spinal Cord Stimulation
sources.авторы: Kimberley Ladner; Eline M. Versantvoort; Marjolein E.G. Thijssen; Dave Mugan; Stuart N. Baker; Alexander Kraskov; Quoc C. Vuong; Mahima Sharma; Marom Bikson; Birte E. Dietz; Stefano Palmisani; Ilona Obara
sources.модальность: Epidural spinal recordings during SCS (ECAP, doublet = secondary/tertiary ECAP, ESAP, EMG) in rats and macaques
sources.задача: Characterize waveform, recruitment thresholds, amplitudes, latencies and conduction velocities of epidural SCS-evoked signals (ECAP, doublets, ESAPs, EMG), compare them across rat and macaque, and discuss their putative physiologic origins and biomarker potential for SCS; no pain or clinical-outcome prediction
sources.метод: Anesthetized preclinical SCS: 18 male Sprague-Dawley rats with two eight-electrode custom epidural paddle leads (L2-T12 and T11-T6, 4 mm spacing) received monopolar biphasic stimulation (200 us, 2 or 50 Hz) stepped to motor threshold from each electrode while non-stimulating electrodes recorded; 2 male rhesus macaques had one 12-electrode epidural lead (T11-L3, 7 mm spacing) with tripolar triphasic 10 Hz (100 us) or tripolar biphasic 3 Hz (80 us) pulses up to ~3x ECAP threshold. Signals analyzed for thresholds, amplitude, latency, distance-latency slopes (conduction velocity) and propagation using custom MATLAB toolboxes; amplifier blanked during stimulation, no offline filtering. Includes a literature synthesis table (Table 1).
sources.датасет: In-house preclinical recordings: 18 male rats (ECAP in 18/18; ESAP in 4/18; doublet in 1/18; EMG in 1 representative rat) and 2 male rhesus macaques (ECAP and doublets in 2/2; EMG in 1 representative animal; no ESAP observed). Pilot slow-wave observations in sheep and bovine are mentioned in the Limitations as unpublished context, not as a reported dataset. No deposited dataset; data available from the corresponding author on reasonable request (Data Statement).
sources.производительность: Descriptive physiology, no predictive or outcome metric: ECAP threshold 32.00 +/- 3.10 uA (rats, n=18/18) and 375.00 +/- 25.00 uA (macaques, n=2/2); ECAP conduction velocity 30.70 +/- 1.81 m/s (rats, n=18) and 82.75 +/- 2.46 m/s (macaques, n=2); secondary ECAP (doublet) threshold 143 uA (n=1 rat) and 550/950 uA (n=1 each macaque), tertiary ~700 uA (n=1); doublet conduction velocity 33.62 m/s (rat, primary 15.28 m/s) and 81.54 / 108.07 m/s (macaques, primaries 54.81 / 46.74 m/s), tertiary 79.49 m/s; secondary ECAP 1.65 ms (rat) and 1.36 ms (macaque) after the primary ECAP; ESAP threshold 91.00 +/- 12.00 uA (n=4 rats), S1 latency ~3-4 ms and duration ~6 ms, non-propagating with a spatial maximum over L1/T13; EMG threshold 245 uA (rat) and 900 uA (macaque), 3-5 ms after the stimulus, non-propagating.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable
sources.ограничения: Preclinical mechanistic characterization only. Signals were recorded in healthy, anesthetized, male animals without experimentally induced neuropathic pain, so no human ECAP-outcome link and no documented transfer to human: the paper proposes biomarker hypotheses and explicitly calls for future neuropathic-pain and awake-animal studies. ESAPs appeared in only 4/18 rats and were absent in macaques; doublets appeared in 1/18 rats and 2/2 macaques, so those conduction-velocity values are single-subject. All animals were male and anesthetized (the authors note unpublished evidence that anesthesia shifts ECAP threshold and latency). No predictive model, calibration or held-out validation; no performance comparison with human SCS data; the sheep/bovine slow-wave observations are unpublished pilot context. Data are only available on request.

sources.название: A modular, high-bandwidth, bidirectional implantable device for neural interrogation
sources.авторы: Radu Darie; Samuel R Parker; Jonathan S Calvert; Ekta Tiwari; Naser Abdelrahman; Sohail Syed; Elias Shaaya; Jared S Fridley; Mark W Merlo; Ian Halpern; David A Borton
sources.издание: Journal of Neural Engineering 23(4):046020, IOP Publishing; published online 2026-07-14
sources.модальность: Implanted bidirectional neural interface: 64-channel electrophysiological recording and 16-channel current stimulation with UWB telemetry; ovine epidural spinal ECAP with synchronized hindlimb EMG
sources.задача: Demonstrate a fully implantable, modular, high-bandwidth bidirectional interface (Modular Bionic Interface, MBI) that connects to third-party neural probes; validate recording and stimulation on the benchtop and during chronic ovine implantation
sources.метод: MBI = implanted unit plus magnetically aligned worn unit. Implant: FPGA (ICE40LP8K) control, Intan RHD2164 64-channel amplifier, four CSI021 current sources (16 stimulation channels), 102 IO pads, three 24-contact Sygnus connectors, HD64 ASIC for the actively multiplexed Micro-Leads HD64 epidural array. Telemetry: in-house 65 nm LPE CMOS UWB ASICs, 3.1-5.1 GHz (4.056 GHz centre), DS-CDMA with 1.352 GHz chipping rate; host control via USB 3.0 and a C++ API.
sources.датасет: Benchtop characterization (frequency sweep, replayed intracortical LFP, resistive stimulation loads, wireless-power distance sweep) plus one chronically implanted Polypay sheep bearing a third-party HD64 epidural spinal array. Data: OSF doi 10.17605/OSF.IO/9HXWE; code: github.com/rdarie/modular-bionic-interface-2026. No human participants; no patient-level pain dataset.
sources.производительность: Telemetry up to 104 Mbit/s raw (96.5 Mbit/s effective); the reported in vivo configuration sampled 64 channels at 37 kHz (~38 Mbit/s), with the remaining bandwidth filled by a dummy stream. Recording matched RHD2164 bandwidth and reproduced replayed intracortical LFP/spikes. Stimulation delivered 10 us-1.28 ms pulses at 600 uA-3 mA with two independent contacts at 175 Hz and 90 Hz. Wireless power worked over 0-22.5 mm, drawing 9.47-10.76 W. In vivo: stable communication across three months in one sheep; peripheral TENS-evoked spinal ECAPs (n=50 pulses, ~10 ms latency) with EMG (~20 ms); SCS-evoked ECAPs (n=15 trials, 300 ms train, 2.1 mA). Descriptive device performance only, no predictive metric.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_reported
sources.ограничения: Device/engineering demonstration, not a pain study. The in vivo work is a single sheep (n=1); the Discussion states the testing was within a single sheep and that additional testing is needed before clinical translation. No human participants, no human ECAP-to-outcome link, and no transfer or validation in humans. Recorded ECAPs are evoked spinal field potentials, not a pain measure, and no analgesia, pain-intensity or SCS-efficacy endpoint is reported. No cross-animal or cross-subject validation and no independent replication. The accessible full text is the bioRxiv author manuscript v1, which reports three months of implantation, whereas the IOP version of record abstract reports six months; the version-of-record full text itself was not readable (paywalled, CAPTCHA). Several authors are shareholders of Modular Bionics Inc.

sources.метод: Hybrid computational model: FEM volume conductor of the lower thoracic spine in COMSOL (mesh in 3-matic, literature conductivities) coupled to multicompartment sensory axon models in NEURON; 100 dorsal-column positions by axon diameters 6.0-15.9 um in 0.1 um steps (10,000 axons); reciprocity-based calculation of ECAPs at the recording contacts; parameter sweeps over dCSF thickness, recording pairs, pulse width, IPI, biphasic/triphasic waveforms, four stimulation configurations and 50-1000 Hz
sources.датасет: No new experimental data and no public data or code deposit stated in the checked text. Model geometry, tissue conductivities and fiber morphometry come from literature; a human clinical ECAP dataset is used only to match the median model bipolar electrode impedance (911 ohm).
sources.производительность: Simulated results only. dCSF 1->5 mm raised ET/DT by about 640% (1.2->8.9 mA and 1.7->12.5 mA). Pulse width 90->300 us lowered ET/DT by about 60% and delayed N1/P2 peaks by 0.22-0.30 ms. Guarded-cathode had the lowest thresholds (ET/DT 3.6/5.0 mA) versus wide-bipolar 3.7/5.2 and bipolar 3.8/5.3 mA. 50->1000 Hz raised ET from 3.7 to 5.3 mA and active fibers at DT by about 246% (1547->5353) while mean ECAP amplitude fell about 50% (20.7->8.8 uV). Similar ECAP amplitudes could mask differences in underlying recruitment.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable
sources.ограничения: In-silico study with no enrolled participants or animals and no patient-linked SCS, analgesia or pain outcome. Model ECAPs exclude electrical and biological noise (stimulation, movement, respiratory and EMG artifact). Dorsal rootlets, axon trajectory variability and patient-specific anatomy, tissue properties and lead placement are not modeled; anatomy is an averaged literature-based FEM. The human ECAP dataset enters only as an impedance-matching scalar, not as an outcome. No independent human ECAP recording is used to validate the model, so no transfer to human ECAP morphology, recruitment or clinical dose control is established. ECAP is not a direct measure of pain.

sources.название: A generalized activating function for rapid and accurate neural response prediction in spinal cord stimulation
sources.авторы: Taylor H. Newton; Javier García Ordóñez; Abdallah Alashqar; Vincent Gemar; Andreas Rowald; Jocelyne Bloch; Grégoire Courtine; Niels Kuster; Esra Neufeld
sources.издание: Communications Biology (Article in Press, 2026; volume, issue and article number not assigned at check date)
sources.модальность: Simulated extracellular potential, subthreshold membrane polarization, axon activation thresholds and spike-initiation location/timing (in-silico only)
sources.задача: Rapid and accurate prediction of SCS-evoked neural activation (axon recruitment thresholds and spike initiation) and its use for pulse-waveform and multipolar electrode optimization
sources.метод: Generalized activating function (GAF): convolution of the extracellular potential with a Green's-function kernel (FFT) capturing subthreshold membrane polarization including axial-current diffusion, leakage and pulse shape; threshold-crossing criterion with calibrated critical voltage Vc; verified against NEURON multi-compartment (MRG/SENN) simulations; PyTorch automatic-differentiation multipolar optimization and Dakota MOGA Pareto pulse-waveform search
sources.датасет: No new human data: patient-specific lumbosacral reconstruction (700 myelinated double-cabled axon models; 16-contact epidural paddle lead) reused from Rowald et al. Per-figure input/source data and analysis scripts deposited at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20139935; NEURON reference models on ModelDB
sources.производительность: GAF vs NEURON over 7000 paired observations (700 axons x 10 pulse widths): activation-threshold R2 = 0.99 (classical AF R2 = 0.14), spike-time R2 = 0.91, spike-location R2 = 0.98; median threshold difference 2.3% (IQR 1.1-3.5%); up to ~1000x and ~260x speedups; Pareto pulse optimization ~7x energy efficiency; multipolar selectivity index 82% vs 52% clinical benchmark. In-silico comparison, not clinical efficacy
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable
sources.ограничения: In-silico methods paper: no human ECAP recording, no patient-linked ECAP or outcome link, and no clinical-outcome or human-transfer validation. The GAF is restricted to the subthreshold regime and does not model conduction block, refractoriness or other active-membrane dynamics; calibrated Vc was not invariant for short pulses and sub-internodal source-fiber separations. A single reused patient-specific anatomy is modeled; individual-patient validation is not demonstrated. Code (s4l_neurfunctions) is proprietary to Sim4Life, limiting independent rerun.

provenance.query_or_seed: 10.1038/s42003-026-10849-x generalized activating function SCS neural response prediction

evidence.population: Computational lumbosacral spinal-cord model with 700 myelinated double-cabled axon models, derived from a previously published human MRI reconstruction (Rowald et al.); no newly enrolled participants
evidence.target_label: Model-predicted axon activation thresholds, spike-initiation location and timing, dorsal-root recruitment and functional selectivity index; no ECAP waveform, pain or clinical outcome is measured

validation.notes: Publisher 'Article in Press' accepted-manuscript PDF (17 pp.; HTTP 200, 2026-09-30) read in full: abstract, Results (GAF verification, Rowald et al. reproduction, multipolar and pulse-waveform optimization), Discussion/limitations, Methods and Data/Code availability. The GAF is verified only against NEURON multi-compartment simulations and a computational reproduction of Rowald et al.; no human ECAP, pain or SCS treatment outcome is measured or linked and no independent external cohort is used. The checked version is an accepted manuscript subject to replacement by the final Version of Record; PubMed and Europe PMC had not indexed the record by DOI or exact title at check date.

sources.название: Computational modeling of paresthesia generated by spinal cord stimulation using a percutaneous lead
sources.авторы: Tom Le Tutour; Karim El Houari; Maxime Billot; Michel Rochette; Arnaud Germaneau; Philippe Rigoard
sources.модальность: Computed paresthesia maps from a two-step in silico SCS simulation (finite-element electric field, MRG axon ODEs, PAM50-based thoracolumbar geometry, percutaneous lead); no measured human paresthesia or ECAP.
sources.задача: Build a parametrizable computational model that computes SCS-induced paresthesia maps for a percutaneous lead, so that spatial targeting and programming parameters can be studied in silico.
sources.метод: Two-step simulation workflow: the electric field in the spinal cord and surroundings is computed with the Finite-Element Method (FEM) on a geometry based on a section of the PAM50 spinal-cord template; axon effects are then assessed with Ordinary Differential Equations. Somatotopy is represented explicitly by the fiber trajectories, and beta myelinated dorsal-column and dorsal-root fibers are modelled with the McIntyre-Richardson-Grill (MRG) double-cable model. Lead laterality and rostro-caudal placement are varied.
sources.датасет: No participant dataset. Anatomy from a section of the PAM50 spinal-cord template; no enrolled cohort and no measured paresthesia maps are reported. Publisher data-availability statement (landing page): the data cannot be made publicly available because they are not in a sufficiently accessible or reusable format; available on reasonable request from the authors.
sources.производительность: Qualitative only at the checked access level: the computed paresthesia maps generally follow expected projections for lead laterality and rostro-caudal placement, with additional rostro-caudal placement effects at a vertebral level reported as interesting and left to the discussion. No numerical accuracy, agreement, concordance or clinical-effect metric is readable here; the article body, figures and tables are behind the publisher access wall.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable: single in silico proof-of-concept model; no enrolled participants and no participant-level split or held-out-subject evaluation.
sources.ограничения: In silico proof-of-concept only. No enrolled patients, no measured paresthesia and no ECAP are recorded, and no link from computed paresthesia maps to human ECAP, pain intensity or clinical SCS response is tested; the paper itself calls the maps a step towards clinical validation. Only the publisher landing page (title, byline, affiliations, dates, abstract, data-availability statement) and registry metadata could be read: direct publisher access returned a bot-challenge page and no OA full text exists, so model parameters, numerical results, figures and robustness checks are unverified. Anatomy is one template (PAM50) with an arbitrary somatotopic distribution; only beta dorsal-column and dorsal-root fibers are modelled; postural lead migration and patient-specific anatomy are not covered. The underlying data are not publicly reusable.

sources.название: Neurophysiological and Psychophysical Biomarkers for Predicting Spinal Cord Stimulation Treatment Response in Chronic Neuropathic Pain: A Systematic Review
sources.авторы: Charles A. Odonkor; Richard Fagbemigun; Fatimah B. Alhassan; Alaa Abd-Elsayed
sources.модальность: Systematic review of human pre-treatment and intraoperative EEG, MEG, SSEP/CHEP, QST, CPM and therapy-embedded ECAP biomarkers of SCS response
sources.задача: Evaluate whether objective pre-treatment or intraoperative neurophysiological and psychophysical biomarkers predict SCS treatment response in adults with chronic neuropathic pain
sources.метод: Pre-registered (PROSPERO CRD420261410302) PRISMA 2020 systematic review; six databases plus ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP searched to 4 June 2026; dual independent Rayyan screening (kappa 0.94 on a 100-record calibration sample, 0.61 on 206 title/abstract records), duplicate extraction, QUIPS/PROBAST/QUAPAS risk of bias, narrative SWiM synthesis (pre-specified meta-analysis not feasible)
sources.датасет: 12 included peer-reviewed studies published 2000-2026, analyzed N per study 12-180 (median about 22), predominantly FBSS/radicular neuropathic pain; no new participant-level dataset (search strategies, excluded full texts and PRISMA checklist in Supplementary Files S1-S3)
sources.производительность: Apparent/internal performance only: MEG ML classification 76% accuracy; intraoperative EEG ML 88.2% accuracy, AUC 0.879, F1 0.857; no included model had external validation. Historical SSEP cohort (2003, n=95): normal dorsal-column central conduction 75.4% success versus near-zero when abolished. ECAP closed-loop neural-dose regimen (n=180) about 79% maximal analgesic effect. All 12 studies at high overall risk of bias.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable: systematic review without a subject-level prediction model
sources.ограничения: Review of a small, clinically and methodologically heterogeneous human evidence base: analyzed N 12-180, all 12 studies at high overall risk of bias, meta-analysis not feasible, no contacted authors, no funnel plots or GRADE tables, and two recent EEG cohorts from one center may share participants. No included model was externally validated. sources.метод: Systematic review with searches of MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL and WikiStim; dual independent study selection, data extraction and Quality in Prognosis Studies risk-of-bias assessment; narrative synthesis without meta-analysis

The review pools no individual patient data and hides no causal claim of its own; associations are not causal. It links no human ECAP measure to any SCS outcome, so it provides no human ECAP-outcome link and does not transfer to ECAP-based or any other neural-biomarker prediction of SCS response. Findings stay at the study level and cannot be moved to an individual patient.

sources.название: First evidence of a biomarker-based dose-response relationship in chronic pain using physiological closed-loop spinal cord stimulation
sources.авторы: Leah Muller; Jason Pope; Paul Verrills; Erika Petersen; Jan Willem Kallewaard; Ian Gould; Dean M Karantonis
sources.издание: Regional Anesthesia & Pain Medicine 50(4):345-351; online 19 March 2024
sources.модальность: ECAP neural-dose device telemetry (neural activation, percent usage over ECAP threshold, dose ratio, dose accuracy) linked to patient-reported percent pain reduction
sources.задача: Test whether objective ECAP-derived neural metrics of therapy dose, usage above the neural activation threshold and dose accuracy are associated with pain reduction in physiologic closed-loop (ECAP-controlled) SCS, and report first evidence of a dose-response relationship in SCS for chronic pain.
sources.метод: Retrospective analysis of real-world device data pooled from FDA/ethics-approved EVOKE/PCLCS studies and commercial use; for each patient the visit of maximal analgesic effect was selected and percent usage over ECAP threshold, dose ratio and dose accuracy were binned into four groups and tested for trend against percent pain reduction with a one-tailed Jonckheere-Terpstra ranked test; Spearman rank correlations between metrics; two retrospective case studies.
sources.датасет: Real-world global EVOKE-system database from FDA/ethics-approved clinical studies (EVOKE, ECAP, AVALON, BRIGHTON, DR, DURABILITY, FRESHWATER) and commercial settings: 690 unique subjects, January 2017 to June 2023; participant-level data are not published (available on reasonable request).
sources.производительность: Percent usage over ECAP threshold (p<0.01), dose ratio (p<0.01) and dose accuracy (p<0.03) each show a significant positive relationship with percent pain reduction under a four-group Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test; percent time the stimulator was on is not significant (p>0.05). Spearman r2: dose ratio vs percent time above ECAP threshold 0.81, dose ratio vs dose accuracy 0.16, percent time above threshold vs accuracy 0.07 (all p<0.001). Grouping counts and per-group medians are given in Figure 2.
sources.кросс_субъект: not_applicable: retrospective population-level association study, not a predictive model
sources.ограничения: Retrospective, post hoc analysis: patients were not assigned to dose ratios, usage categories or accuracy levels, so no causal dose assignment and only natural variability is exploited. Data points come from different per-patient timepoints (selected maximal-analgesic-effect visit; follow-up ranges from months to years). No independent external cohort or prospective replication, no participant-level data release (available on reasonable request). Funded by Saluda Medical, with three authors (LM, IG, DMK) employed by the manufacturer; Saluda Medical is the device maker (EVOKE System). ECAP-derived metrics are a neural dose/recruitment signal, not a direct measurement of pain. Percent pain reduction is patient-reported and the design cannot separate dose effects from selection, placebo or programming effects.

evidence.population: Adults with chronic pain implanted with the EVOKE ECAP-controlled physiologic closed-loop SCS system across FDA/ethics-approved clinical studies and commercial settings.
evidence.target_label: Percent pain reduction at the maximal-analgesic-effect visit, related to objective ECAP neural metrics (percent usage over ECAP threshold, dose ratio, dose accuracy); patient-reported pain reduction, not an ECAP-only measurement.

validation.notes: Primary open-access full text checked via Europe PMC PMC12015077 fullTextXML (HTTP 200, CC BY-NC 4.0) on 2026-09-30; the BMJ publisher route (https://rapm.bmj.com) returned HTTP 403 locally and Crossref plus PubMed/Europe PMC were used for bibliographic confirmation. Verified: 690 unique subjects (2017-2023, EVOKE System, Saluda Medical), three ECAP neural metrics versus patient-reported percent pain reduction with a four-group Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test, and two retrospective case studies. The human ECAP-to-pain link exists but is observational and correlational: doses were not assigned, the analysis is post hoc, there is no independent external validation or split, follow-up timepoints differ per patient, and the study is funded by the device manufacturer. ECAP metrics quantify neural recruitment/dose and are not themselves a direct measure of pain. Participant-level data are not released. No transfer to a Drosophila or computational model is claimed. Cross-checked against the related corpus records S236 and S237 (ECAP-controlled closed-loop SCS, real-world pain outcomes); no duplicate DOI/PMID/title exists in the canonical corpus.
